notes: Cold means empty application cache, not cleared upstream caches.
Real HTTP requests use the production handler and checker with an isolated SQLite file.
Benchmarked production source is unchanged throughout the run.
Detailed and basic requests use different application cache keys.
Additional warm passes exclude unknown responses because unknown results are not cacheable.

metric_definitions.quantiles: Hyndman-Fan type 7 linear interpolation at (n-1)*p; all durations are seconds.
metric_definitions.format_accuracy: Correct format judgments divided by unique cases in a phase; missing-address HTTP400 is a valid malformed rejection.
metric_definitions.classification: Known-used recall is positive on-chain evidence; synthetic absence agreement is an expectation, not absolute proof. Unknown/unusable counts remain separate and are not counted correct in overall agreement.
metric_definitions.age: Coverage is separate from deployment agreement. Earlier-than-deployment observations are ambiguous, and genesis controls have no invented Unix timestamp.
metric_definitions.latency: HTTP client wall time includes local handler/serialization and upstream calls but excludes configured pauses. Empty application cache does not clear provider caches.
metric_definitions.cache: Only conclusive valid results are cacheable; malformed inputs are local rejections. Cacheable results may still lack optional age/count details.
metric_definitions.upstream_errors: Transport errors and HTTP429 are counted from request instrumentation; JSON-level api_status values are separately counted and are not all errors.
metric_definitions.phase_accuracy: Repeated extra passes are deduplicated by case ID for accuracy; timing and request counts include every request.

deployment_comparison.interpretation: Deployment agreement is not a universal first-ever wallet-age accuracy metric; earlier prefunding can be legitimate.
